title: Change the cache headers and watch the outcome
purpose: Predict how max-age, no-cache, no-store, heuristics, s-maxage, Vary and hashed file names change hit, revalidate and miss.
sequence_reason: Each header changes what the cache does at the next request, so the walkthrough pauses on one header at a time while the simulation replays it.
summary: The walkthrough steps through seven cache rules. max-age sets a lifetime; a stale copy revalidates with If-None-Match. no-cache stores but always revalidates, while no-store never stores. Without max-age a cache may guess about 10% of the time since Last-Modified. s-maxage gives shared caches such as a CDN their own lifetime. Vary keeps one copy per request header value. Hashed file names with a one-year max-age and immutable get a new cache key on every build.
explanation: Every scene loads a matching preset in the simulation, so you can step through the same rule request by request.

learning_check.question: Why does a new hashed file name always cause a miss, even when the old file is cached for a year?
learning_check.answer: The cache key includes the URL. A new name is a new URL, so the cache has no stored copy for it.

scenes.heading: Change one header at a time
scenes.narration: Now change the headers yourself. Each scene loads a matching preset in the simulation beside the player.

scenes.heading: max-age=60 over two minutes
scenes.narration: With max-age set to sixty, requests at thirty and fifty-nine seconds are a HIT. At ninety seconds the copy is stale, so the cache must revalidate.

scenes.heading: Stale copy: If-None-Match, then 304
scenes.narration: The stale copy carries ETag v1. The cache sends If-None-Match v1. The origin answers 304, and the copy is fresh again.

scenes.heading: no-cache is not no-store
scenes.narration: no-cache stores the response but revalidates before every reuse. no-store never stores it, so every request goes to the origin.

right.label: no-store
items: Every request goes to the origin

visual.verdict: no-cache means check first, not do not store

scenes.heading: No max-age: a heuristic guess
scenes.narration: With no max-age and no Expires, a cache may guess a lifetime. A common guess is ten percent of the time since Last-Modified.

terms.note: a typical guess, not a fixed rule
modified 10 days ago gives about 1 day

scenes.heading: s-maxage is for shared caches
scenes.narration: A CDN is a shared cache. For shared caches, s-maxage overrides max-age, so the CDN keeps the copy fresh for ten minutes.

scenes.heading: Vary: one copy per header value
scenes.narration: Vary Accept-Encoding makes the cache keep one copy per encoding. A gzip request cannot reuse the br copy.

items: br request: MISS, store the br copy
gzip request: no match, MISS, store the gzip copy
br request: HIT on the br copy

scenes.heading: Hashed names: a new build is a new URL
scenes.narration: app.3f9a1c.js never changes, so it gets max-age of one year and immutable. A new build gets a new name, so a new cache key.

items: Every visit: HIT, no trip to the origin
New URL, new key: MISS, fetch once
